key_sub: The long hand shows the minutes.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The short hand shows the hour; the long hand shows minutes in steps of 5.
  • a.m. is before noon; p.m. is after noon.
  • 7 days = 1 week, 12 months = 1 year.

Examples

Example

The hour hand is just past 4 and the minute hand points to 3.

3 × 5 = 15 minutes

Answer: 4:15

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading the hands the wrong way roundShort hand: hour. Long hand: minutes.
Counting the 12 as 12 minutesAt 12 the minutes are 0.

What do a.m. and p.m. mean?
faq.a: a.m. is from midnight to noon; p.m. is from noon to midnight.

items.q: The digital clock shows a time. How do we say it?
items.e: 8:35 is 35 minutes past 8. That is more than half past, so say to the next hour. 60 − 35 = 25 minutes to 9: 25 to 9.

The short hour hand is between 6 and 7, so the hour is still 6. The long minute hand points to 10. Count in 5s: 10 × 5 = 50 minutes past. That is 10 minutes before 7 o’clock (60 − 50 = 10). The minute hand is on the left-hand side, so we say to 7. It is 10 to 7.

The short hour hand is between 12 and 1, so the hour is still 12. The long minute hand points to 1. Count in 5s: 1 × 5 = 5 minutes past. The minute hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past 12. It is 5 past 12.

items.q: The digital clock shows a time. How do we say it?
items.e: 4:20 is 20 minutes after 4 o’clock. It is less than half past, so say past: 20 past 4.

The short hour hand is between XI (11) and XII (12), so the hour is still 11. The long minute hand points to VII (7). Count in 5s: 7 × 5 = 35 minutes past. That is 25 minutes before 12 o’clock (60 − 35 = 25). The minute hand is on the left-hand side, so we say to 12. It is 25 to 12.

items.q: The digital clock shows a time. How do we say it?
items.e: 2:50 is 50 minutes past 2. That is more than half past, so say to the next hour. 60 − 50 = 10 minutes to 3: 10 to 3.

The short hour hand is between 2 and 3, so the hour is still 2. The long minute hand points to 11. Count in 5s: 11 × 5 = 55 minutes past. That is 5 minutes before 3 o’clock (60 − 55 = 5). The minute hand is on the left-hand side, so we say to 3. It is 5 to 3.

items.q: The digital clock shows a time. How do we say it?
items.e: 11:40 is 40 minutes past 11. That is more than half past, so say to the next hour. 60 − 40 = 20 minutes to 12: 20 to 12.

items.e: Midnight is 12 o’clock at night, when one day ends and the next day starts.
am times go from midnight to noon (night and morning). pm times go from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening).
The afternoon is after noon, so it is a pm time. 2:30 am is in the middle of the night. So the answer is 2:30 pm.

items.q: Which is a sensible time for school to start?
items.e: School starts in the morning, so it is an am time. 3:50 am is the middle of the night. So the answer is 8:50 am.
Midnight is 12 o’clock at night. 11:50 pm is 10 minutes before midnight. 11:50 am is 10 minutes before noon. So the answer is 11:50 pm.

items.q: It is 11:30 am. What time will it be 1 hour later?
items.e: 1 hour after 11:30 is 12:30. It is now after noon, so it changes to pm: 12:30 pm. (12:30 am is just after midnight.)

The short hour hand is between 5 and 6, so the hour is still 5. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 8. Count in 5s to 40, then on in 1s: 44 minutes past. It is after noon, so it is pm. So it is 5:44 pm.

The short hour hand is between 3 and 4, so the hour is still 3. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 4. Count in 5s to 20, then on in 1s: 22 minutes past. It is after noon, so it is pm. So it is 3:22 pm.

The short hour hand is between 12 and 1, so the hour is still 12. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 4. Count in 5s to 20, then on in 1s: 24 minutes past. It is after noon, so it is pm. So it is 12:24 pm.

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 9. Count in 5s to 45, then on in 1s: 49 minutes past. It is the morning, so it is am. So it is 8:49 am.

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 2. Count in 5s to 10, then on in 1s: 12 minutes past. It is the morning, so it is am. So it is 7:12 am.

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 3. Count in 5s to 15, then on in 1s: 16 minutes past. It is after noon, so it is pm. So it is 7:16 pm.

items.q: Write 20 past 10 in the morning as a digital time.
items.e: “20 past 10” means 20 minutes after 10 o’clock: 10:20. It is in the morning, so it is am: 10:20 am.

items.q: Write 25 to 9 in the morning as a digital time.
items.e: “25 to 9” means 25 minutes before 9 o’clock. 60 − 25 = 35, so it is 35 minutes past 8: 8:35. It is in the morning, so it is am: 8:35 am. (Not 9:35 am: that is after 9 o’clock.)

items.q: Write 20 to 5 in the afternoon as a digital time.
items.e: “20 to 5” means 20 minutes before 5 o’clock. 60 − 20 = 40, so it is 40 minutes past 4: 4:40. It is in the afternoon, so it is pm: 4:40 pm. (Not 5:40 pm: that is after 5 o’clock.)

items.q: Write 5 to 8 in the evening as a digital time.
items.e: “5 to 8” means 5 minutes before 8 o’clock. 60 − 5 = 55, so it is 55 minutes past 7: 7:55. It is in the evening, so it is pm: 7:55 pm. (Not 8:55 pm: that is after 8 o’clock.)

items.q: On a 24-hour clock, what is 3 pm?
items.e: pm times are after noon. Add 12 to the hour: 3 + 12 = 15. So 3 pm is 15:00.

items.q: A 24-hour clock shows 18:30. What is this in 12-hour time?
items.e: Take away 12 from the hour: 18 − 12 = 6. It is in the evening, so it is 6:30 pm. (Do not just drop the 1: 18:30 is not 8:30.)

items.q: How is midnight shown on a 24-hour clock?
items.e: On a 24-hour clock a new day starts at midnight, so midnight is 00:00. 12:00 is noon.
There are 60 seconds in 1 minute.
There are 60 minutes in 1 hour. (Not 100: time does not count in hundreds.)
There are 24 hours in 1 day: 12 am hours and 12 pm hours. 12 + 12 = 24.
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday: 7 days. (5 is just the school days.)
January to December: 12 months. (52 is the number of weeks.)

items.q: How many days are in a year that is not a leap year?
items.e: A normal year has 365 days. A leap year has 1 more: 366.

items.q: How many days are in a leap year?
items.e: A leap year has 1 extra day, 29 February. 365 + 1 = 366 days.

items.q: How many days does February have in a normal year?
items.e: February is the shortest month. It has 28 days, and 29 days in a leap year. It never has 30.

items.q: In a leap year, how many days does February have?
items.e: In a leap year February gets 1 extra day: 28 + 1 = 29 days.
Remember: “30 days has September, April, June and November. All the rest have 31, except February.” So September has 30 days.

items.q: What day of the week is September 1, 2,027?
items.e: Find the 1 on the calendar. Look up its column to the day name: Wednesday. (Not Sunday: the month does not always start in the first column.)

items.q: Today is Monday, October 4. What is the date 1 week from today?
items.e: 1 week is 7 days. 4 + 7 = 11, so it is Monday, October 11. (October 14 counts a week as 10 days.)

items.q: Today is Wednesday. What day will it be in 3 days?
items.e: Count 3 jumps: Wednesday → Thursday → Friday → Saturday. (Friday counts today as one of the days.)

items.q: The green box is Siddharth’s first day of school. What day of the week is it?
items.e: The box is around the 7. Look up the column: it is a Tuesday. So the first day of school is Tuesday, September 7.
April, June, September and November have 30 days. March, July and August have 31 days. So the answer is April.

items.q: Jasleen’s school has its Charity Run on the circled day. What is the date?
items.e: The red circle is around the 23. Look up the column: it is a Thursday. So the date is Thursday, September 23.
February is the shortest month. In 2,027 it has 28 days. (It has 29 days only in a leap year, such as 2,028.)

items.q: How many Wednesdays are in September 2,027?
items.e: Look down the Wed column: 1, 8, 15, 22, 29. That is 5 Wednesdays. (Many months have 4, but count to be sure.)

items.q: Which month comes 3 months after November?
items.e: Count 3 jumps: November → December → January → February. (January counts November as one of the months.)

items.q: BC Day is a holiday on the first Monday in August. What is the date of BC Day in 2,027?
items.e: Look down the Mon column. The first Monday is the 2nd. So BC Day is Monday, August 2. (August 1 is a Sunday. August 9 is the second Monday.)

items.q: A TV programme starts at 4:10 pm and ends at 4:35 pm. How long is it?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 35 − 10 = 25 minutes.

items.q: Rohan starts reading at 7:05 pm and stops at 7:45 pm. How long does he read for?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 45 − 5 = 40 minutes.

items.q: Morning break starts at 10:30 am and ends at 10:45 am. How long is break?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 45 − 30 = 15 minutes.

items.q: Varun’s piano lesson is from 5:20 pm to 5:50 pm. How long is the lesson?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 50 − 20 = 30 minutes.

items.q: Assembly starts at 9:05 am and ends at 9:27 am. How long is assembly?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 27 − 5 = 22 minutes.

items.q: A football match starts at 2:45 pm and ends at 3:30 pm. How long is the match?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 2:45 pm to 3:00 pm is 15 minutes. Then 3:00 pm to 3:30 pm is 30 minutes. 15 + 30 = 45 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: Rohan gets on the school bus at 8:40 am. He gets to school at 9:05 am. How long is the bus ride?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 8:40 am to 9:00 am is 20 minutes. Then 9:00 am to 9:05 am is 5 minutes. 20 + 5 = 25 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: Rehan’s swimming lesson is from 3:50 pm to 4:35 pm. How long is it?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 3:50 pm to 4:00 pm is 10 minutes. Then 4:00 pm to 4:35 pm is 35 minutes. 10 + 35 = 45 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: A cake goes in the oven at 11:48 am. It comes out at 12:13 pm. How long does it bake?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 11:48 am to 12:00 pm is 12 minutes. Then 12:00 pm to 12:13 pm is 13 minutes. 12 + 13 = 25 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: A film starts at 5:50 pm and ends at 7:20 pm. How long is the film?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 5:50 pm to 6:00 pm is 10 minutes. Then 6:00 pm to 7:20 pm is 1 hour 20 minutes. 10 + 80 = 90 minutes = 1 hour 30 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)
Both times are in the same hour. 30 − 15 = 15 minutes.

items.q: Gym class starts at 1:05 p.m. and ends at 1:45 p.m. How long is gym class?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 45 − 5 = 40 minutes.
Both times are in the same hour. 35 − 10 = 25 minutes.

items.q: Anika starts the Charity Run at 1:15 p.m. She finishes at 1:52 p.m. How long does she take?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 52 − 15 = 37 minutes.
The minutes are the same, so count the hours. Count the jumps, not the numbers: 9:00 a.m. → 10:00 a.m. That is 1 hour. (1 hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Simran’s family hikes in Stanley Park from 1:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. How long is the hike?
items.e: The minutes are the same, so count the hours. Count the jumps, not the numbers: 1:00 p.m. → 2:00 p.m. → 3:00 p.m. That is 2 hours. (1 hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Recess starts at 10:15 a.m. It lasts 15 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Count on 15 minutes from 10:15: 15 + 15 = 30. It is still the morning, so recess ends at 10:30 a.m. (11:15 a.m. would be 1 hour later.)

items.q: The bus for the field trip to Science World leaves at 9:35 a.m. It gets there at 10:20 a.m. How long is the bus ride?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 9:35 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 25 minutes. Then 10:00 a.m. to 10:20 a.m. is 20 minutes. 25 + 20 = 45 minutes. (Not 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Shreya rides the SkyTrain from 3:45 p.m. to 4:10 p.m. How long is the ride?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 3:45 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. is 15 minutes. Then 4:00 p.m. to 4:10 p.m. is 10 minutes. 15 + 10 = 25 minutes. (Not 65 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)

items.q: Nikhil’s swimming lesson is from 4:45 p.m. to 5:20 p.m. How long is it?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 4:45 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. is 15 minutes. Then 5:00 p.m. to 5:20 p.m. is 20 minutes. 15 + 20 = 35 minutes. (Not 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just subtract the numbers.)
